test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jul, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To throw dust in one’s eyes

options.text: To talk in an abusive language

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To throw dust in one’s eyes"** means **to mislead or deceive someone by tricks or false information.** (किसी को धोखा देना)

 
 
• **Example:** The conman **threw dust in the old man's eyes** by pretending to be a bank officer.
 
 
 
• **Mislead** refers to causing someone to have a wrong idea or impression about something. (गुमराह करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The advertisement was designed **to mislead** consumers about the product's benefits.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***To mislead someone by tricks**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: To talk in an abusive language** (गाली देना)

 
 
• **Example:** He was known to talk in an abusive language whenever he got angry.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To hit someone with stone** (किसी को पत्थर से मारना)
 
 
• **Example:** The angry mob decided to hit the thief with stones.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To make someone blind forever** (किसी को हमेशा के लिए अंधा कर देना)
 
 
• **Example:** The accident made him blind forever.
 
 

55:Tb69,
The correct answer is **Option 1)**
